body:
Did you use AI tools in the development of this PR? Please note that must be disclosed, see https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html

(Closed prematurely because of suspicious verbiage and looking like automated spam, but realized on a closer read it wasn't, apologies!)

Hi everyone, and thank you very much for taking the time to review my first contribution and for the feedback so far!

I also want to thank you for reopening the PR after the initial misunderstanding. I realize now that my description was much longer than what is usually expected. Since this is my first contribution to Godot, I wanted to provide as much context as possible and also introduce myself a little. I understand that I overdid it, and I'll make future PR descriptions much more concise and focused on the technical changes.

I genuinely appreciate corrections and review comments. They help me learn how the project works and how to contribute in a way that fits Godot's development process. My goal is to keep improving and, together with everyone here, continue making Godot more accessible.

For some context, I am totally blind and I rely on screen readers every day while programming. I have spent many hours testing Godot with NVDA, Windows Narrator, and AccessKit, which has given me a good understanding of the accessibility issues that affect real-world development workflows. Many of the ideas in this PR come directly from that daily experience.

Regarding AI tools: yes, I did use AI during the development of this PR. I mainly used it for brainstorming ideas, improving documentation, organizing descriptions, and speeding up some parts of the development process. However, I made a conscious effort to review and understand every change myself. I manually implemented, tested, debugged, and validated the accessibility behavior using screen readers before submitting this contribution, and I take full responsibility for everything included in this PR.

Thank you again for your time, your patience, and your feedback. I'm looking forward to learning from your reviews and continuing to contribute to Godot's accessibility.

Thank you and exciting contribution for very important features!

Please note that we do not accept significant amounts of AI authored code (regardless of testing and proofreading) and we do not accept AI written documentation at all

Hi @bruvzg, thank you very much for the review and for pointing that out.

Sorry about that. I was experimenting with that part, and I forgot to remove the Android-specific AccessKit adapter before opening the PR.

In another branch I already have that part working together with the Java bridge, but I intentionally didn't include it here because I think it belongs in a separate contribution once that work is ready.

Just to make sure I follow the expected workflow correctly: should I remove the Android adapter for now, carefully review the code style issues, update this PR, and then request another review? Or would you recommend a different approach?

Thanks again for taking the time to review my contribution. I really appreciate the feedback and I'm looking forward to learning the project's workflow better.

Thank you very much for the clarification and for explaining the project's policy. I really appreciate it.

To be completely honest, I did use advanced AI agents during the development of this PR to help accelerate parts of the implementation, explore different approaches, and assist me throughout the development process. However, I manually reviewed, tested, debugged, and validated the behavior myself, especially using NVDA, Windows Narrator, and AccessKit, since accessibility is something I rely on every day.

Regarding the documentation, I did not simply generate it and submit it as-is. I wrote and expanded it myself, although I also used AI to help improve wording and organization. I understand now that this does not align with the project's policy, and I will make sure that future PR descriptions and documentation are written entirely by me.

I'm still learning how Godot's contribution process works, so I truly appreciate you taking the time to explain these expectations. My main goal with this contribution was to bring forward ideas and improvements that I believe are essential for real accessibility with screen readers, based on my daily experience as a blind developer.

Thank you again for your patience and for helping me learn the project's workflow. I genuinely appreciate the guidance, and I'll keep it in mind for future contributions.
